newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down, central bank sells dollars.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down, central bank sells dollars.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Tuesday, despite the central bank's dollar sales, on the view that the dollar was still undervalued, dealers said.
The won closed at 868.80 after opening at the day's high of 867.10. It touched a low of 869.10, which was the lowest level since the market average system was introduced in March 1990.
"Dollar strength will continue given piling trade deficit," said a domestic bank dealer. The dollar's rise against the yen on world markets also prompted the won's fall, he said.
South Korea posted a record trade deficit of $3.48 billion in January against a $2.13 billion shortfall a year ago.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 868.60 on Wednesday, compared with 866.80 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the Bank of Korea sold dollars twice, at 868.50 in early morning trade and at 869.00 in late morning.
"Dollar demand appears too strong for the central bank to fight," said a foreign bank dealer.
Dealers forecast trading would range from 868.00/40 to 869.70/80 on Wednesday.
